races.title: State Senate, District 48
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Tim Moffitt
cands.bio: Republican member of the North Carolina Senate for District 48 since 2023. Owns a management consulting firm, Moffitt International. Previously served in the state House for District 116 (2011-2015) and District 117 (2020-2023); appointed to the District 117 seat in October 2020.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Moffitt was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. We found no documented statements or actions from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, land purchases by investors or foreign buyers, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B visas, policing, guns, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no endorsements for the 2026 race; Ballotpedia lists none. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys, so his campaign themes are not on record there. We found no news coverage or controversy reporting about him.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Served in the NC House 2011-2015 and 2020-2023 and in the NC Senate since 2023. Owns the management consulting firm Moffitt International. Committee assignments have included Finance and Appropriations.
qual.why: He has about a decade of prior legislative service and runs a consulting business. Committee seats and chairs were not counted toward the score.
qual.label: He has about a decade of prior legislative service and runs a consulting business. Committee seats and chairs were not counted toward the score.

cands.name: Doyle G. Brown, Jr.
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for North Carolina Senate District 48 in 2026. Small business owner working in affordable housing and other real estate and business ventures. Holds a bachelor's in accounting and an MBA from Delaware State University. Has not held elected office, according to the pages reviewed.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists a voter guide recommendation from the Sway voting group "Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress" (Vote for Peace).
Ballotpedia lists a voter guide recommendation from the Sway voting group "Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy" (Tevin Davis).

cands.gaps: We could not find where Brown was born or raised, or when he moved to North Carolina. We found no record of elected office or legislative work. His business background comes only from his own campaign site, with no independent confirmation of the business or its work. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no documented stances on data centers, development, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, immigration or H-1B, policing, abortion, or teacher pay. His site says all children should be educated whether in public, private or charter schools, but takes no clear position on vouchers or school-choice funding. No news coverage, controversies or foreign ties were found.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Self-described small business owner in affordable housing and real estate, with a bachelor's in accounting and an MBA from Delaware State University. No elected or legislative office was found.
qual.why: Business ownership falls in the middle range for this office. No legislative, policy or budget-office record was found, and the business background comes only from his own campaign site.
qual.label: Business ownership falls in the middle range for this office. No legislative, policy or budget-office record was found, and the business background comes only from his own campaign site.

clean-money.evidence: Says he is running to stop corporations from bribing politicians with donations and that North Carolina needs to get money out of politics. His slogan is "Your Street, Not Wall Street."

second-amendment.evidence: Says Second Amendment rights are guaranteed, but supports "sensible limits," no gun rights for criminals or terrorists, and larger "No Gun Zone" buffers around schools.
